🇲🇽🇻🇪 MEXICO SENDS 71.2 TONS TO EARTHQUAKE-HIT VENEZUELA WHILE WASHINGTON KEEPS SANCTIONING IT

After the June 24 earthquakes, Mexico has delivered 71.2 tons of humanitarian aid to Venezuela — food, 13.1 tons of medicine, and 8 power plants with solar arrays — plus 250 Yumare rescuers who pulled survivors from the rubble and gave 1,411 medical consultations. A Navy ship sails Thursday with more. This is what South-South solidarity looks like: not blockades, not "maximum pressure" — trucks, medics, and lights.

🚨🇲🇽 MICHOACÁN HOMICIDES DOWN 46% — AND THE STATE IS GUARDING ITS LIME AND AVOCADO FARMERS

Michoacán's daily homicide average fell from 4.32 in January 2025 to 2.33 in June 2026 — a 46% drop, the lowest June since 2015. But the real tell is where Sheinbaum's Plan Michoacán put its people: 860 troops guarding lime growers, 820 guarding avocado producers, because extortion of farmers is what bleeds this state. 1,300 arrested for high-impact crimes, 1,400 guns seized. Security as protection of the people who feed the country — not occupation.

NY POST/AOL: Mexico pushes to extend USMCA after Trump says he'd 'rather have it terminated'
July 1, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Headline casts Mexico as the anxious petitioner "pushing" to save the deal. 🇲🇽 But Sheinbaum says Mexico already signed the 16-year extension, and Canada completed its step too — it's Washington sitting on the paperwork. The party blowing up the $2 trillion pact is the one that wrote the headline's other half.

Trump negotiated USMCA himself in his first term; now he "may sign it" — or not. Mexico's the stable actor here.

• Trump: "I would rather not have the agreement, but I may sign it"
• Greer: US will "address the Agreement's shortcomings and our trade deficits"

BLOOMBERG: Sheinbaum Approval Falls to New Low as Pocketbook Concerns Bite
July 3, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Bloomberg headlines Sheinbaum "below 50% for the first time" — 49% in a single AtlasIntel/LatAm Pulse poll, down from 53%. 🇲🇽 Same month, Pew found Mexico was the only country surveyed where views of the US improved, and Mexican pollsters have consistently placed her 10-20 points higher.

One outlier survey commissioned by Bloomberg itself becomes the story; the pollsters showing her comfortably in the 60s don't get a headline.

• "dipped below 50% for the first time"
• down "to 49% in June from 53% a month earlier"

BROBIBLE: Did Mexico Cartel Threaten Ecuador Soccer Players To Lose At The World Cup?
July 2, 2026 | 🤡

🤡 An Argentine pundit floated that a Mexican cartel threatened Ecuador's players and their families so Mexico would win. No player, no relative, no outlet confirmed a word of it. FIFA said the one-hour delay was thunderstorms. Mexico won 2-0 on the field.

The only real "incident" was Mexican fans honking horns outside Ecuador's hotel — over which Ecuador filed a FIFA complaint. That became "cartel threat" in the retelling.

• claim: "cartel wanting Mexico to become World Cup champion at all costs"
• FIFA: delay was "due to thunderstorms and lightning"

THE NATIONAL INTEREST: While the World Wants Oil, Mexico Stays on the Sidelines
July 3, 2026 | 🟡

📰 The National Interest scolds Mexico for "staying on the sidelines" while other countries drill for export markets. 🇲🇽 Sheinbaum isn't chasing global barrels — she's stabilizing Pemex for domestic supply and building toward 70% clean power by 2030. Not maximizing oil exports during a climate crisis is a choice, not a failure.

The piece leads with Pemex's $2.6B Q1 loss but never mentions Mexico's renewable buildout or that oil-export maximalism is exactly what the planet can't afford.

• "decades of mismanagement of the oil sector"
• "content to let other countries go after global markets"

🇲🇽📈 <u>THE SUPERPESO CLIMBS AGAIN — ON AMERICA'S WEAKNESS</u>

The peso closed at 17.47 per dollar, strengthening again — this time because the US jobs report collapsed: just 57,000 new jobs in June, roughly half the forecast, with May revised down from 172,000 to 129,000. Bets on Fed rate cuts sank the dollar. Mexico's currency keeps gaining on Washington's cooling economy, not on any trouble of its own.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S OPPOSITION CAUGHT PUSHING AN AI DEEPFAKE TO SMEAR AMLO</u>

Mexico's opposition got caught circulating an AI-generated fake video to attack AMLO — so blatant that even figures in their own camp called for it to be taken down. The family targeted called the smear "indignant and shameful," demanded evidence or a public apology, and is weighing legal action. When you have no record to run on, you manufacture one.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SAME FUNDERS, SAME SCRIPT: THE SOFT COUP AGAINST SHEINBAUM</u>

Contralínea maps the destabilization network aimed at Sheinbaum: USAID and NED money, the Atlas Network, Vargas Llosa's foundation, CPAC, and the PAN old guard — Calderón, Fox, Cortés — running what the report calls "a new offensive phase of limited chaos," the same playbook deployed against Venezuela, Bolivia and Cuba. Same money, same NGOs, same script. Mexico has seen this movie.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>DEATH BY PAPERWORK: THE NETWORK CHOKING THE TREN MAYA</u>

A Contralínea investigation finds 70 environmental cases against the Tren Maya still open — 24 of them on the main line — kept alive for up to 5 years, with the agency pushing "millionaire fines" routed toward a private trust tied to Julia Carabias and José Sarukhán, both longtime opponents of the project. Officials insist the permits are "100% in place." The files just never close.
